segments: the lord of Egypt.
One of his father's slaves was made king over Egypt,
a man whose name was Izz al-Din the Turkmen.
And he took the wife of his master as his wife,
her who was called Shajar al-Durr,
a Turkish bondwoman.
And when some time had passed,
on one of the days, when he entered the bathhouse to wash,
she sent some of her young slaves, and they strangled him,
because she perceived that he wished to destroy her.
And there arose after the Turkmen in Egypt a Turkish slave of his, whose name was Qutuz {OCR?}, and he was called al-Malik al-Muzaffar.
And he killed Shajar al-Durr,
and cast her corpse to the dogs,
that is to say, as one avenging the blood of his master.
Yet in truth,
it was because he was afraid that she might kill him
that he killed her.
Otherwise he would not have destroyed her,
for she was famous for feminine beauty and for manly conduct.
And at this time, when al-Malik al-Nasir, the lord of Aleppo, saw
that slaves were ruling in Egypt
and killing one another as if by chance {OCR?},
he gathered his forces and went up to Damascus,
and took possession of it peacefully, in tranquility and without battle.
Now when Batu, the son of Jochi, the son of Genghis Khan, set out from his camp which was in the country of Saqsin and the Bulgars to go to visit Guyuk Khan,
and arrived at a place called Ala-Qamaq, near the city of Qayaliq,
the report of the death of Guyuk Khan reached him.
Therefore he remained in his place,
and sent envoys to all the royal princes,
and gathered them to him.
And those who were not able to come
sent letters, saying:
"Batu is the head of all of us,
and whatever he does,
we consent to it and accept it."
At first, indeed, the sons of Guyuk Khan, together with the queen their mother, whose name was Oghul Qaimish {OCR?} Khatun, came to Batu,
and stayed for only two days.
And they left and departed,
leaving behind Temur Noyan, and they said to him:
"When the royal princes, great and small, are assembled,
whatever they agree upon,
you also agree to on our behalf."
And when their assembly was complete,
they all committed the choice to Batu:
that if he wished to be [khan],
he should be;
and if not, whomever he chooses,
all of us will submit to."
